messages:
maria: Quick check — REST vs gRPC for the control plane routes? Thinking about telemetry propagation, quota enforcement, and console rollout UX.
jon: +1 for a quick sync. what's driving the re-check? :thinking:
maria: Our gateway is getting messy: multiple serializers, ad-hoc header mappings, and the console needs deterministic schemas for rollout diffs. Also worried about schema drift if we keep JSON-first.
kevin: From perf side gRPC has better p99s with persistent connections. But browser + public operators will expect REST/JSON. I lean gRPC between services, transcode at the gateway.
sara: Product here — iteration speed matters. JSON is easier to prototype. But if proto -> json-schema generator exists we could get the best of both worlds.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for "gateway-v2-transcode" (canary=3%) :rocket:
jon: Concrete idea: define canonical protobufs for routing + quota metadata. Compile-time validation for services, and an automated transcode layer that exposes OpenAPI for operator-facing endpoints.
kevin: Sounds fine. Two implementation cautions: 1) schema evolution — add-on fields must be optional, and 2) avoid client breakage during rollout. Use one-way compat rules.
sara: Console UX: we need flat, human-friendly shapes. If we autogenerate json-schema from proto we can render forms and show diffs. That fits our rollout signal needs.
maria: Quota enforcement is sticky — edge (envoy/gateway) should be the source of truth for immediate enforcement. But envoy often needs a lightweight quota service to consult. We should standardize the quota proto so envoy can call it directly.
jon: Agree, but watch latency. Envoy gRPC calls to quota service add tail risk. Mitigation: local caching in gateway + async reconciliation.
kevin: On the control plane traffic pattern: most calls are short unary RPCs, not streaming. Prefer unary gRPC to avoid head-of-line issues if we multiplex different tenants on streams.
sara: Ops question: will transcode duplicate quota checks (gateway + backend)? We must ensure single-count semantics. Prefer gateway to record/consume tokens once.
maria: We can expose a small quota-check proto and let envoy be authoritative. Backends can do best-effort double-checks for safety only.
jon: Schema rollout plan: proto-first, allow minor changes (add optional fields). For breaking changes, use versioned RPCs and route-weighted canaries in console.
kevin: For telemetry, we need consistent header propagation (trace/tenant). Propose a small header mapping middleware that normalizes trace/tenant headers before transcode.
sara: Also want per-route telemetry surfaced in the console: token usage, error rates, rollout signal. If proto drives the UI, diffs are easy to generate and annotate.
maria: Action items: 
- kevin: spike gRPC unary control-plane + gateway transcode (2d)
- jon: proto -> json-schema generator + sample UI form (3d)
- sara: define header conventions + envoy filter mapping (1d)
- maria: write short runbook clarifying quota ownership and counting semantics (1d)
jon: I'll create a PR template for proto changes to force compatibility checks.
kevin: I'll add a microbench in infra/controlplane/proto-poc and measure p50/p99 vs JSON-over-HTTP.
sara: Ping @maria when the canary finishes so we can validate UI signals.
maria: Thanks everyone, this feels actionable. :thumbsup:
